annotation.title_clean: Tanggungjawab Perubatan dalam Pembedahan yang Dibantu Robot Menurut Perspektif Etika Islam dan Fiqh
annotation.title_en: Medical Responsibility in Robot-Assisted Surgery from Islamic Ethical and Fiqh Perspectives
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Yunos, A. S.; Wan Saifuddin, W. M. S.; Hamdan, M. N.; Baharudin, M. H.
named_instruments_referenced: Resolutions of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed Malay-language article analysing medical liability in robot-assisted surgery (e.g. da Vinci) through Islamic ethics and fiqh. It allocates ethical, criminal (qisas, ta'zir) and contractual/compensatory (daman) responsibility among surgeons, medical teams, manufacturers, hospitals and maintenance engineers, and proposes a Shariah-compliant accountability model.
key_provisions_or_claims: Medical responsibility in robotic surgery is legal liability borne by doctors or equivalent parties in the form of qisas, ta'zir or daman
Liability is allocated using the classical distinction between direct causation (mubasharah) and indirect causation (tasabbub)
Manufacturers, hospitals, medical teams and maintenance engineers share liability according to their role and the type of negligence
Hospitals must provide accurate marketing, sterilisation, adequate training and data accuracy, and are liable for negligence in these areas
An Islamic accountability framework ensures justice, patient safety and trustworthiness
